newsitem.title: FRANCE: Anomalous to exclude EMU members on decimals - OECD.
newsitem.headline: Anomalous to exclude EMU members on decimals - OECD.

text.p: OECD chief economist Stephen Potter said on Thursday that from an economic point of view, it would be anomalous to exclude countries from European monetary union on the basis of public deficits which were a few decimal points wide of the Maastricht mark.

"The decision will be political. (But) from an economic point of view, it would seem anomalous to exclude a few countries on the basis of a few decimal points," Potter told reporters at a briefing after the OECD released economic forecasts including deficit forecasts for EU countries.
Potter said he was talking about countries whose public deficits were going in the right direction.
The OECD Economic Outlook released earlier on Thursday forecast a public deficit equivalent to 3.2 of gross domestic product in 1997 for Germany, France and Italy.
It forecast Italy's deficit growing in 1998, but Germany's and France's deficits hitting or going under the three percent Maastricht target.
